title: Together AI Pricing 2026: Serverless & Dedicated GPUs
summary: Together AI pricing bills by tokens for serverless and GPU hours for endpoints.
body_markdown:
## Fix Surprise AI Bills with Activepieces Spend Alerts


Run a scheduled check on your usage, compare it to a budget you wrote down, and let Activepieces tell you in[Slack](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/slack) or email when you're over.


A daily check is one run, so 1 credit a day, about 30 of the 1,000 credits the free plan includes each month. That matters most on a self-hosted GPU that keeps billing while nobody uses it.


It doesn't change how Together AI bills you, and it can't set a hard cap. Nothing in the workflow stops spend by itself; it shortens the time between a meter running and a person noticing.


Activepieces has an MIT-licensed core, as the LICENSE file in its GitHub repository states, and can be self-hosted, so the checker can run on infrastructure you already pay for rather than adding another per-task subscription to the bill you are trying to shrink.


On Activepieces Cloud, the pricing page publishes 1 credit per flow run however many steps it has, where Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's bills per module, so a ten-step checker costs the same as a two-step one, and the free plan includes 1,000 credits a month.


### What the workflow checks and when


On the builder canvas, the workflow below is a three-step flow. It starts with a Schedule trigger labeled "Every Day," passes to a Code action that picks what to check, and ends in an HTTP action that makes the outbound call.


Read it as the skeleton: a clock, a bit of logic, and a request. Your version swaps the last step for a call to whatever usage source you have access to.


Metered here is a run of the flow, one per day in this setup. A daily schedule means an overspend can go up to a day before anyone hears about it, so a team with an expensive dedicated endpoint may want a tighter interval.


Before you pick a tighter interval, check how your plan or your own server counts runs, since a tighter interval means more of them.


Look to the Code step for the budget. It takes the usage figure, compares it to the number you set before launch, and decides whether to notify.


Keeping that comparison in one visible step means anyone on the team can read the threshold and change it, instead of finding it buried in a vendor dashboard.


Once the comparison fails, the next step posts to Slack or sends an email, with the endpoint name and the amount over budget in the message. A vague alert gets ignored; one that names the endpoint can be acted on.


### Approval step before shutting down Together AI endpoints


For idle dedicated endpoints, the flow can pause and ask a person before it shuts anything down. The approval step sends a message with the endpoint and its idle time, and the shutdown call runs only if someone approves.


That pause is deliberate. An automatic shutdown can take down an endpoint a teammate is about to use, and a surprise outage costs a different kind of money.


A human decision keeps the savings and removes the risk of a script making the wrong call at night.
